title: Carías Andino Ends 16-Year Dictatorship as Gálvez Takes Office
reason: Carías left office December 31, 1948; Gálvez took power January 1, 1949. The transition occurred in 1949, not 1950. Year is off by 1+.

title: United Fruit and Standard Fruit Control Honduras's Banana Economy
reason: Well-documented; United Fruit and Standard Fruit controlled vast concessions on Honduras's north coast through the mid-20th century.

title: Great Banana Strike Paralyzes Honduras for 69 Days
reason: Strike began April 1954, lasted 69 days, involved over 25,000 workers. Confirmed via Wikipedia and multiple academic sources.

title: CIA Uses Honduras as Base for Operation PBSUCCESS Against Guatemala
reason: CIA established training camps in Honduras; Honduras served as staging ground for the 1954 Guatemalan coup.

title: Honduras Enacts First Labor Code Following the Great Strike
reason: A 'Constitution of Labor Guarantees' (Decree-Law No. 50) was issued February 16, 1955, but Honduras's actual Labor Code (Decree No. 189) was enacted in 1959. Describing the 1955 decree as the 'First Labor Code' is materially wrong.

title: Military Coup Ousts President Lozano Díaz, Installs Junta
reason: Coup on October 21, 1956; three-man military junta installed. Confirmed via Wikipedia.

title: New Constitution Adopted, Villeda Morales Wins Presidency
reason: Constituent Assembly elected Villeda Morales November 16, 1957; constitution embedded military role as institutional guardian. Confirmed.

title: Villeda Morales Launches Agrarian Reform and Social Security System
reason: IHSS (social security) and INA (agrarian reform) established under Villeda Morales. Confirmed.

title: Military Coup Removes Villeda Morales Days Before Scheduled Elections
reason: Coup occurred October 3, 1963, ten days before scheduled elections. Confirmed via Wikipedia.

title: Land Pressure Intensifies as Peasant Organizations Mobilize for Reform
reason: ANACH peasant mobilizations and land disputes are documented; causal link to Football War tensions is established in the literature.

title: Football War with El Salvador Kills Thousands, Destroys Regional Integration
reason: Four-day war in July 1969; estimated 1,000–6,000 deaths, hundreds of thousands displaced. OAS brokered ceasefire. Confirmed.

title: General López Arellano Returns to Power, Pursues Agrarian Reform
reason: Coup on December 4, 1972, ousted Ramón Cruz. Second government pursued agrarian reform including Decree 8 (1973). Confirmed.

title: Hurricane Fifi Devastates North Coast, Killing Over 8,000
reason: Hurricane Fifi struck September 1974; estimated 8,000–10,000 deaths; banana plantations destroyed. Confirmed.

title: Bananagate Scandal: United Brands Paid $1.25 Million Bribe to Honduran Officials
reason: United Brands paid $1.25 million to Honduran officials to reduce banana export tax. SEC investigation confirmed; led to ouster of López Arellano. Note: bribe exposed/paid in 1974–75, scandal broke April 1975.

title: Los Horcones Massacre: Landowners Murder Fourteen Peasant Activists
reason: June 1975, Olancho; up to 15 killed including two priests. Confirmed via Wikipedia. Description says 'fourteen' — Wikipedia says 'up to 15'; minor discrepancy but within range.

title: Sandinista Victory in Nicaragua Transforms Honduras's Cold War Strategic Position
reason: Sandinistas overthrew Somoza July 1979; Nicaraguan Guardsmen regrouped in Honduras forming Contra nucleus. Confirmed.

title: Honduras Becomes Staging Ground for CIA-Backed Contra Forces
reason: CIA organized Contra forces in Honduras from early 1980s with Honduran military cooperation. Confirmed.

title: Honduras Returns to Civilian Rule as Suazo Córdova Wins Elections
reason: Elections November 29, 1981; Suazo took office January 27, 1982. First civilian transfer since 1963. Confirmed.

title: Battalion 316 Death Squad Established with CIA Training
reason: Battalion 316 established by Álvarez Martínez with CIA/Argentine training; 184 documented disappearances. Confirmed via Wikipedia and HRW.

title: US Military Constructs Permanent Infrastructure for Contra Operations in Honduras
reason: Joint Task Force Bravo at Palmerola; permanent infrastructure built under guise of exercises. Confirmed.

title: Iran-Contra Scandal Exposes Extent of US Covert Operations Run Through Honduras
reason: Scandal broke November 1986; Honduras hub of covert Contra supply network. Confirmed.

title: Central American Peace Plan (Esquipulas II) Creates Framework for Ending Regional Conflicts
reason: Five Central American presidents signed Esquipulas II 1987; Arias won Nobel Prize. Confirmed.

title: Inter-American Court Rules Against Honduras in Landmark Velásquez Rodríguez Case
reason: Judgment July 29, 1988; first Inter-American Court ruling on state responsibility for disappearances. Confirmed.

title: Callejas Implements Structural Adjustment Program, Privatizing State Enterprises
reason: Callejas launched SAP in 1990 with IMF/World Bank; privatization, trade liberalization, inflation hit 36.4%. Confirmed.

title: Contra Forces Demobilize as Central American Peace Process Concludes
reason: Sandinistas lost February 1990 elections; UN-supervised Contra demobilization followed. Confirmed.

title: Maquiladora Export Processing Zones Expand Rapidly Near San Pedro Sula
reason: Maquiladora expansion under Caribbean Basin Initiative well documented in the 1990s. Confirmed.

title: Reina Wins Presidency on Anti-Corruption and Human Rights Platform
reason: Carlos Roberto Reina won 1993 election; abolished mandatory military service; transferred police to civilian control. Confirmed.

title: Truth Commission Documents 184 Disappearances by Honduran Security Forces in the 1980s
reason: National Human Rights Commissioner documented 184 disappearances attributable to Battalion 316. Confirmed via HRW.

title: US Deportations Begin Introducing Gang Culture into Honduran Cities
reason: US deportations of gang members from LA introduced MS-13/Barrio 18 structures to Honduras. Confirmed.

title: Hurricane Mitch Devastates Honduras, Killing Over 5,000 and Setting Development Back Decades
reason: Mitch hit October 1998; ~7,000 deaths in Honduras; $5 billion in damage; president cited '50 years of progress' lost. Event says 5,000+ — confirmed (actual figure ~7,000, so 5,000+ is accurate). Confirmed.

title: United States Grants Temporary Protected Status to Hondurans Post-Mitch
reason: TPS designated January 5, 1999 by Clinton; covered ~60,000–72,000 Hondurans. Confirmed.

title: Mano Dura Anti-Gang Policy Criminalizes Gang Membership
reason: President Ricardo Maduro enacted mano dura legislation criminalizing gang membership. Confirmed.

title: Honduras Signs CAFTA-DR Free Trade Agreement with the United States
reason: Honduras signed CAFTA-DR in 2004; entered into force 2006. Confirmed.

title: Manuel Zelaya Wins Presidency, Honduras Shifts Leftward
reason: Zelaya won 2005 election; joined ALBA; aligned with Chávez. Confirmed.

title: Drug Trafficking Cartels Expand Presence in Honduras as Key Cocaine Transit Country
reason: Sinaloa Cartel and Los Zetas expansion in Honduras as transit corridor well documented. Confirmed.

title: Military Coup Ousts President Zelaya, Triggering International Crisis
reason: Coup June 28, 2009; Zelaya flown to Costa Rica; OAS suspended Honduras July 5, 2009 under Article 21. Confirmed.

title: San Pedro Sula Becomes One of the World's Most Violent Cities
reason: San Pedro Sula recorded homicide rate exceeding 100/100,000 around 2010–2013. Confirmed.

title: Berta Cáceres Begins Organizing Lenca Communities Against Agua Zarca Dam
reason: COPINH campaign against Agua Zarca began circa 2011; Goldman Prize won 2015; IFC and Sinohydro withdrew. Confirmed.

title: Aguan Valley Land Conflict Kills Dozens of Peasant Activists
reason: At least 60 activists murdered in Aguan Valley 2009–2012 per Global Witness. Confirmed.

title: Comayagua Prison Fire Kills 361 Inmates in Worst Prison Disaster in Honduran History
reason: Fire February 14–15, 2012; 361 deaths; 852 inmates in facility designed for 250. Confirmed.

title: Juan Orlando Hernández Wins Presidency, Beginning Authoritarian Consolidation
reason: Hernández won 2013 election; later convicted in US of drug trafficking. Confirmed.

title: Surge of Unaccompanied Honduran Child Migrants Reaches US-Mexico Border
reason: 57,000+ unaccompanied minors from Northern Triangle apprehended FY2014; Hondurans were largest group. Confirmed.

title: IHSS Corruption Scandal Implicates Ruling Party, Triggering Mass Protests
reason: $200M+ stolen from IHSS; funds diverted to Hernández's 2013 campaign; Indignados protests confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Supreme Electoral Tribunal Removes Constitutional Bar on Presidential Re-election
reason: Constitutional chamber struck down re-election ban in 2015; enabled Hernández's 2017 bid. Confirmed.

title: Indigenous Leader Berta Cáceres Assassinated in La Esperanza
reason: Shot dead March 2, 2016 (event says March 3 — one-day discrepancy, not a year-off). Location La Esperanza confirmed. DESA executives linked to killing confirmed.

title: Hernández Wins Disputed Re-Election Amid Massive Fraud Allegations and Deadly Protests
reason: Contested November 2017 election; OAS called for new elections; ~30 demonstrators killed (event says 'at least 22' — undercount but not materially wrong). Confirmed.

title: Migrant Caravans from Honduras Draw International Attention to Forced Displacement
reason: October 2018 caravans confirmed; driven by gang violence and poverty; triggered US political controversy. Confirmed.

title: US Federal Prosecutors Name Hernández as Drug Trafficking Co-Conspirator
reason: US prosecutors named Hernández as co-conspirator in December 2019 filings; Sinaloa Cartel bribe allegations confirmed. Confirmed.

title: Hurricanes Eta and Iota Strike Honduras Within Two Weeks, Causing Catastrophic Flooding
reason: Category 4 Eta (November 3), Category 4/5 Iota (November 16–18); ~74–100 deaths in Honduras; widespread displacement. Confirmed.

title: David Castillo Convicted of Co-Authoring Berta Cáceres Assassination
reason: David Castillo found guilty July 5, 2021 of co-conspiring in Cáceres murder. Confirmed.

title: Xiomara Castro Wins Historic Presidential Election, Ending National Party Rule
reason: Castro won November 28, 2021 with ~53% of votes; first female president; ended 12 years of National Party rule. Confirmed.

title: Former President Hernández Extradited to United States on Drug Trafficking Charges
reason: Hernández extradited April 2022; indicted in SDNY; convicted March 2024; sentenced 45 years. Confirmed.

title: Honduras Switches Diplomatic Recognition from Taiwan to China, Joins Belt and Road
reason: Honduras broke with Taiwan March 2023; established PRC relations; joined Belt and Road June 2023. Confirmed.

title: Former President Hernández Convicted on All Counts, Sentenced to 45 Years
reason: Convicted March 8, 2024 on three counts; sentenced June 26, 2024 to 45 years. Event says 'sentenced to 45 years' — confirmed. Court was SDNY (not Southern District as described, which is correct). Confirmed.

title: Trump Administration Threatens TPS Termination for Hundreds of Thousands of Hondurans
reason: Trump administration moved to terminate Honduras TPS in 2025; ~72,000 Hondurans affected; remittances exceed 25% of GDP. Confirmed.
